ontology.note: Emits an fw:NetworkReachability activity carrying fw:originCount, fw:reachedNodeCount, fw:travelBudgetMetres, fw:travelBudgetMinutes, fw:assumedSpeedMetresPerMinute, fw:travelMode, fw:travelDirection, fw:edgeLengthSource and, when origins were left out or routed across unmapped ground, fw:unconnectedSiteCount, fw:unconnectedSites, fw:offNetworkSiteCount and fw:offNetworkSites, and prov:used the site source. When it attaches origins to the network itself, it also carries fw:attachedOriginCount, fw:attachmentLimitMetres when a limit is set, and the metric CRS it measured nearest in.

changes.description: The Preview says exactly what it is waiting for, and never asks for something already connected. It was `minutes x speed` -- "That goes up to 800 m along the streets from each site" -- arithmetic on the two numbers just typed, identical whether the network reaches a thousand junctions or none. The budget sentence stays, and what it buys is now counted by `reachableNodes` where the sites and the network can both be read. A downloaded network is held outside the page by reference and read when the workflow runs, so that is said in place rather than asking the reader to connect a network that is already there.

evidence.note:
Eleven unit checks cover junctions inside a 200 m budget being returned and a 300 m one not; travelled plus remaining equalling the budget at every junction; the cheapest route deciding the cost, where a 400 m direct street loses to 100 plus 100 through a third junction; inbound and outbound differing on a one-way street in both directions; an origin without a networkNodeId failing with a message naming the snap step; an origin snapped to a different network being refused rather than dropped; per-origin sets tagged by origin; the constant speed and the trusted street lengths both appearing in the notes; a node beyond the budget being discovered but never settled; refusal of an impossible budget, speed, direction or label; a speed outside its mode's plausible band being refused in both directions, where 400 m/min labelled walking is reported as 24 km/h against a 1.8 to 6.6 km/h band; the 1854 Soho 75 m/min sitting inside the walking band, since that is where the band came from; public transport being refused with its reason; and the mode and the km/h travelling in both the notes and the receipt. One check runs the real composition: snapping then reachability over the 738-node Soho network the John Snow example ships, at its own 5 minutes and 75 m per minute, reaching 142 junctions. Not established: that the reached set is what anyone can actually reach. Parity against NetworkX ego_graph with distance='length' is not done. 0.6.0: tests/reachable-inspector.browser.mjs through Configure… and Apply; Chromium, 2026-11-23.

THE PREVIEW (2026-11-25). Browser tested on Chromium: tests/reachable-inspector.browser.mjs asserts the two waiting messages, including that a connected-but-unreadable network is named as such. NOT ESTABLISHED, and unexercised: the branch that counts junctions. Every example here holds its street network by reference, so driving it needs a fixture whose network is inline; there is none yet.
